notification.audit_focus: MODULE NOT YET REDESIGNED — only module still carrying #5 + several others.

anti_patterns.name: No property-scope authorization (CRITICAL — only remaining instance)
anti_patterns.evidence: notification_router.py:56-68 GET /history has NO require_property_scope / require_role dependency. notification_service.py:185-191 get_history() checks 'if property_id:' BEFORE 'if user_id:' — so GET /notifications/history?property_id=<victim> returns ANOTHER property's full notification history to ANY authenticated caller. POST /test (notification_router.py:33-48) and PATCH /{id}/resend (notification_router.py:76-87) also only depend on get_current_user — no scope check.
anti_patterns.root_cause: Notification module was never part of the property-scope remediation that touched Auth/Property/Tenant/Contract/Maintenance/Dashboard/Billing. The dependency require_property_scope() exists and is reusable (deps.py:103) but was never applied here.
anti_patterns.recommended_fix: Apply require_property_scope(query_param='property_id') to GET /history and POST /test (body-sourced property_id). For PATCH /{id}/resend, resolve the notification's property_id and user_has_property_scope() check (mirror maintenance_router.py:190-192). Add a test asserting a non-scoped caller gets 403 on ?property_id=<other>.
anti_patterns.effort: M (0.5-1 day: 3 endpoints + service guard + 1 test file)

anti_patterns.name: Ambiguous error handling (fail-silent envelope)
anti_patterns.evidence: notification_router.py:31 docstring 'Fail-Silent — always returns 201'; notification_service.py:79-132 send_test catches all exceptions, sets status=FAILED, never raises. A failed send still returns 201 Created with a 'failed' record.
anti_patterns.root_cause: Fail-silent design choice (intentional per module doc) but collides with REST semantics — caller cannot distinguish success from failure via status code; they must inspect response body status.
anti_patterns.recommended_fix: Either (a) keep 201 but document that body.status tells the real outcome (acceptable for fire-and-forget notifications), or (b) return 202 Accepted + async job if send is genuinely async. At minimum, do NOT claim 201 'Created' when the underlying send failed — consider 200 with explicit status, or surface a partial-failure field. Align with the unified {'error':...} envelope if a hard failure should be reported.

anti_patterns.name: Blocking on long-running task (sync send in request path)
anti_patterns.evidence: notification_service.py:106-110 _mock_external_send is awaited inline in the request path (notification_router.py:40). No 202 + background task/polling pattern. Currently a 0.01s mock, but a real provider (email/LINE/SMS) would block the worker.
anti_patterns.root_cause: Synchronous send; no task queue integration (Celery workers exist in app/workers/ but are unused here).
anti_patterns.recommended_fix: Offload real send to Celery (app/workers/tasks.py) and return 202 Accepted with a status-poll URL; keep the DB record as the source of truth. Low urgency until a real provider is wired.

anti_patterns.name: No idempotency on POST /test
anti_patterns.evidence: notification_router.py:33-48 POST /test accepts no Idempotency-Key (contrast auth_router.py:184, tenant_router.py:55). Re-submitting the same test notification creates duplicate rows.
anti_patterns.root_cause: Newest module; idempotency convention not applied.
anti_patterns.recommended_fix: Add optional Idempotency-Key header on POST /test (reuse idempotency.py). Low urgency for a test endpoint.

prioritized_remediation_plan.action: Add require_property_scope to GET /history, POST /test; resolve-then-check for PATCH /{id}/resend. Blocks cross-property IDOR on notification history.
Decide fail-silent semantics: either keep 201 but document body.status as truth, or move to 202 + Celery async send. Stop returning 201 when send actually failed.
Implement PATCH /admin/config (using UpdateSystemConfigRequest) OR delete the dead schema to avoid a phantom contract.
Source version from settings.APP_VERSION instead of hardcoded literal.
Add Idempotency-Key to POST /test for consistency with other POST endpoints.
Consider per-endpoint limiters beyond login (e.g. invite/register) using existing rate_limit.py pattern; global limiter acceptable for now.
